# Adapter Contract

`adapters/base.py` is the whole interface between the pack and the world. Skills
depend only on these signatures and the shapes they return — never on a concrete
provider. Five adapters implement it today: `jira`, `github`, `linear`, `markdown`,
`openkanban`.

## Mandatory verbs

Nine `@abstractmethod`s. An adapter that omits any one of them cannot be instantiated
at all, which is the intended failure — a half-built adapter must not reach a board.

| Method | Returns | Contract note |
|---|---|---|
| `whoami()` | `str` | the current user's canonical id *for this provider* |
| `list(tier, query)` | `list[Ticket]` | resolves a **named** query from `[queries]`; never takes raw filter text from a caller |
| `view(key)` | `Ticket` | one fully normalized ticket |
| `transition(key, role)` | `None` | takes a **role**, maps it to a lane internally |
| `comment(key, body)` | `None` | posts to the activity stream |
| `blockers(key)` | `list[dict]` | **unresolved only**: `[{"key", "resolved": false}, ...]` |
| `worklog(key, from_role, note, billable)` | `Worklog` | time from the most recent entry into that lane until now |
| `lane_time(key, role, read_only)` | `Worklog` | time across a *closed* lane interval |
| `doctor()` | `list[Check]` | read-only validation of auth, reachability, board model |

Two subtleties that are easy to get wrong:

- `worklog` and `lane_time` are **safe no-ops**, not errors, when
  `[timetracking].provider = "none"` — they return a `Worklog` with `worklog_id=""`.
  Skills render that as "(no time tracking)" and carry on.
- `lane_time(read_only=True)` computes and returns the duration but records nothing,
  and in that mode the timetracking provider is ignored entirely, so a board UI can
  display lane durations on a project that tracks no time.

## Optional verbs

`create`, `apply`, `apply_template`, `edit`, and `link` are **concrete** methods whose
default bodies raise `ProviderError` (exit code 3). That is what lets a backend opt in
one verb at a time without breaking instantiation — see
[`Adapter.create()`](mex://method:e1d19013501e1e28600ffd1601bd468a) for the shape.
Callers branch on the exit code; there is no capability-probing method.

[`Adapter.edit()`](mex://method:da98cb8b89986009045295bfee04d4db) carries the contract's
sharpest rule: **`status` is deliberately not editable.** Lane moves go through
`transition` so board history and worklog timing stay correct. Every other field is
tri-state — omitted (`None`) leaves it unchanged, `""` clears it, a value sets it.

`apply` owns the frontmatter (except `status`) and the body of a canonical ticket
document, while preserving backend-managed sections such as Comments verbatim, and
validates before any write.

## Provided behaviour you inherit

Two methods on the base class are already implemented and should usually be left alone:

- [`lane_time_batch()`](mex://method:a94d5a79663aa921ecd95128c23e0898) loops over
  single `lane_time` calls. Its important property is **partial degradation**: a
  per-key `ProviderError` whose message mentions "no entry" or "no transition" becomes
  a zero-duration `Worklog` rather than aborting the batch; any other error propagates.
  Override it only to make a backend's batch fetch efficient — and preserve that rule.
- [`priorities()`](mex://method:6b98beb8cfdf05978fe7762b49ba2d88) returns the project's
  configured list. Override it only when the backend has its own priority scheme that
  must be reconciled with the configured names (Jira does; nothing else does).

## The normalized shape

[`Ticket`](mex://class:4fa09bc1806974e30fc873f1353a6394) in `core/schema.py`, plus
`Worklog` and `Check`. `to_dict()` is literally `dataclasses.asdict()`, so **adding a
field to the dataclass changes the public JSON contract** that every skill parses.

The fields that carry design intent:

- `status` is the provider's lane string **verbatim**; `status_role` is the canonical
  role resolved from config. Both are present because skills need the role and humans
  need the lane.
- `type_class` is `full_sdlc` | `deliverable` | `unknown`, resolved from
  `[issue_types]`. It is what routes a ticket into the full pipeline versus the
  short-circuit `complete-deliverable` flow.
- `agent_status` is board agent state: `""` | `idle` | `processing` | `waiting` |
  `done` | `blocked`. Only the markdown backend persists it today.
- `due` / `scheduled` / `completed` are `str | None` (ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`), rendering as
  JSON `null` when unset — unlike the string fields, which default to `""`.
- `blocked_by` entries are `{"key": str, "resolved": bool}`; `unresolved_blockers()`
  is the accessor, and the `blockers` verb returns only the unresolved ones.

**The degradation rule:** a backend that cannot store a field leaves it at its
dataclass default. Do not synthesize a plausible value, and do not drop the field.

## Wiring and failure

An adapter reaches the CLI through
[`get_adapter()`](mex://function:0b2b33f8ea63b124544ed4f71236495a), which looks the
provider up in `core/registry.py`'s `_PROVIDERS` and imports the module lazily. A
provider name that is not in that map is a `ConfigError` (exit 2) listing the
available names.

Errors are typed, never sentinels: `ConfigError` 2, `ProviderError` 3 (including
"verb not supported"), `NotFoundError` 4, `UsageError` 64. Raise the right one and the
CLI's central handler does the rest — message to stderr, process exits with that code.
